h: Saltram on screen and in the gardens
p: If Saltram looks oddly familiar, you might have seen it on screen. It played Norland Park in the 1995 film of Sense and Sensibility, starring Emma Thompson and Kate Winslet, and fans of the film enjoy spotting the rooms and views. It's a lovely house to visit with that story in mind.

Art lovers have a treat in store too. The painter Sir Joshua Reynolds was born in nearby Plympton and was a friend of the Parker family, and the house holds a number of his portraits. Standing in front of them in the rooms they were made for is a real pleasure, and a great way to connect the house to its local roots.

Out in the garden, look for the elegant eighteenth-century orangery, along with follies and little buildings tucked away among the trees. In spring, the garden is full of blossom and bulbs, and in autumn the parkland trees put on a colourful show. The paths along the River Plym estuary are popular with dog walkers and joggers, and are mostly gentle and easy-going.

Back in Plymouth, the National Marine Aquarium at the Barbican is a great family add-on, and the Hoe gives you sweeping views over Plymouth Sound. For a bigger outdoor adventure, Dartmoor is only a short drive away, with its tors, ponies and open moorland.

Saltram makes a brilliant change of pace from the city, and you can easily spend a whole day here between the house, garden, parkland and café. If you're visiting with kids, look out for family trails and seasonal activities, which change through the year and help to keep younger visitors interested.
